# mikado

mikado keeps a goal visible while the work behind it grows. A **journey** is a goal crowned by one
quest, its **crowning quest**; the quests it requires, and the quests those require, form a
**chart** from today's work to the goal. You record what you find as you go; the dashboard draws
the chart as a skill tree.

You talk to mikado through its CLI. Every command except `serve` and `skill` is a client of a
local server.

## Before anything

- Run `mikado journey list`. If it fails with "connection refused", the server is not running:
  tell the user to start it with `mikado serve` (it is their long-running process — do not
  start or stop it yourself).
- `mikado help` is the full command reference. Add `--json` to any read command to get
  machine-readable output; prefer it when you need to act on the result (see
  [JSON field names](#json-field-names)).

## The model

- **Quest** (also called a **task** — the two words mean the same): one unit of work on the
  chart: a title and a status you set by hand. mikado reads nothing from outside tools. Two
  optional properties:
  - **link** (`--url`) — any URL: a recipe, a ticket, a document. Never parsed or checked; two
    quests may share one.
  - **mark** (`--mark`) — free text of at most 15 characters, shown right after the quest's id:
    `#13`, `234g45a`, `feat(someh)`, `PROJ-88`. Kept as written, with or without a link.
- **Petition**: a quest with `--on WHO` — something we await a reply on from someone, often
  outside the team ("final key art from the freelance artist"). `mikado set Q --on -` makes it a
  plain quest again.
- **Requires / opens**: "Q5 requires Q3" means Q3 must be fulfilled before Q5; said the other
  way round, Q3 opens Q5. The only blocking link. Cycles are refused.
- **Journey**: a key (e.g. `J2`), a title and a crowning quest. Its quests are *computed*: the
  crowning quest, everything it requires (transitively) — the **main quest** — and their side
  quests. A quest joins a journey by being linked in; it leaves when the link is cut.
- **Side quest**: optional polish hung on a quest (`--side-of`). Never blocks anything; earns an
  achievement, not progress.
- **A journey waiting on a journey**: a quest can require another journey's crowning quest. It
  then waits on that whole journey, which its chart draws as one card with the other journey's
  progress; it counts as one quest there. The other journey's quests stay on their own chart (not
  in this journey's totals, chronicle or `journey show`), unless this journey also requires them
  directly.
- **Status** (computed): *fulfilled*, *open* (everything it requires is fulfilled), *sealed*
  (something it requires is not), *awaiting reply* (an open petition), *abandoned* (won't do:
  stays on the chart, blocks nothing, counts in no total).
- **Underway** is separate from status: `mikado take-up Q` means someone is on it right now;
  `mikado set-down Q` means they stopped.
- **Hero**: who is responsible for a quest, as set in mikado (`--hero`).
- **Region**: a group of journeys (`R2`, with a name). Every journey lives in exactly one, and a
  quest stays inside one: a link that would put a quest on journeys of two regions is refused,
  whether it is a requirement, a crown, a shared quest or a journey waiting on another. A new
  journey goes to the first region (R1, "Personal") unless you name one with `--region`.

## Ids — use them exactly

- A **quest** has one global id, `Q` plus a number: `Q142`. The same quest has the same id in
  every journey. Commands also accept `Q-142`, `q142` or `142`. A mark is not an id: `#13`
  names no quest.
- A **journey** has one id, `J` plus a number: `J7`. It never changes, whatever the title.
- A **region** has one id, `R` plus a number: `R2`; commands also take its name.
- Wherever a quest is expected, a **journey id** names that journey's crowning quest:
  `mikado require Q5 J2`. A journey with no crowning quest yet names none, and the command says
  so.
- When you report back to the user, name quests by their `Q` id (and the mark if it helps) and
  journeys by their `J` id: "Added Q12 (#45) to J2; it opens Q9."
- **mikado ids stay out of anything shared.** mikado is the user's own map; other people working
  in the same repos do not have it, and `Q12` or `J2` means nothing to them. Never write mikado
  ids, journey titles or mentions of mikado into commit messages, branch names, code comments,
  docs, issues, pull requests or review comments. Refer to the work the way the repo does: by
  its own issue or PR numbers, or in plain words. (Example ids in mikado's own docs are syntax,
  not the user's map, and are fine.)

## Workflows

**Start a journey.** Create it, then its crowning quest.

    mikado journey new "The winter update ships to every player"   # prints its id, say J1
    mikado add "Ship the winter update to every platform" --crowns J1

**Chart what the goal requires.** Link each prerequisite to the quest it opens.

    mikado add "Save migration for the winter items" --opens Q1 --mark "#88" \
        --url https://tracker.example/saves/88
    mikado add "Book the store-page feature slot with the platform" --opens Q1 --hero ada

**You found something while working on a quest** — the most important habit. Always say where
it was found and why; that is how the journey's chronicle stays readable.

    mikado add "Old save files crash the loader" --opens Q3 --found-on Q3 \
        --reason "old saves crash the loader"
    mikado add "Final key art from the freelance artist" --on "freelance artist" \
        --opens Q5 --found-on Q5 --reason "placeholder art only; the stores reject it"

**Part of the goal is a whole journey of its own.** When a quest cannot be done until another
goal is reached, and that goal has (or deserves) its own journey — it has its own chart of
quests, other journeys wait on it too, or someone else drives it — link the quest to that journey
by its id instead of copying its quests in. The chart then shows the other journey as one card
with its progress, and the Atlas says which journey blocks which.

    mikado require Q5 J2       # Q5 waits on the whole journey
    mikado add "Record the controller trailer" --requires J2 --opens Q1

Do not do this for optional work (that is a side quest), and do not link a journey to itself or
to a journey that waits on it: requirements stay acyclic and a cycle is refused.

**Optional polish** goes in a side quest, not in the requirements:

    mikado add "Snowfall particles on the title screen" --side-of Q2

**The same quest serves another journey.** Link the quest you have; do not add it again (a
second `add`, even with the same url, makes a second quest):

    mikado require Q40 Q3           # Q3 now opens Q40 too, in both journeys

**Change a quest.** Title, link, mark, petition and hero are set with `set`; `-` clears one.

    mikado set Q3 --url https://tracker.example/saves/88 --mark "#88"
    mikado set Q5 --on "the publisher"   # a petition now
    mikado set Q5 --on -                 # a plain quest again

**Progress.**

    mikado take-up Q7 --by dex    # someone is on it now (underway)
    mikado fulfil Q7                # fulfilled, by hand
    mikado set-down Q7              # stopped without fulfilling it

**Something will not happen.** Abandon it — it stays visible, stops blocking, and its side
quests are abandoned with it. Strike only what should never have been there.

    mikado abandon Q10 --reason "split-screen co-op is cut from this update"
    mikado strike Q11 --reason "added to the wrong journey by mistake"

**Reshape the chart.** Move a requirement in one step with `rewire` — never `unrequire` then
`require`, which lets quests drop out of the journey in between:

    mikado rewire Q5 Q3 Q9          # Q5 requires Q9 instead of Q3

When part of a journey has grown into a goal of its own, extract it. The new journey is crowned
by a new quest with its title, and the old chart shows it as one journey card where the quests
were:

    mikado journey extract J1 Q12 Q15 --title "Save format v2"

**Regions.** Start a journey where it belongs, and keep links inside its region. Journeys that
share quests or wait on each other move together, or not at all:

    mikado region list
    mikado journey new "Ship the store page" --region Work
    mikado region move Work J3 J4 J6

If mikado refuses a link or a move because a quest would cross regions, tell the user what it
said; do not cut links to get a move through.

**Delete** only when the user asks; abandon is usually what they mean. Nothing is left hanging:
if the quest's side quests or prerequisites would leave a journey with it, say what happens to
them — `--branch` takes them along, `--rewire Q` hands them to another quest (it requires the
prerequisites and gets the side quests). A quest leaves the database only with `--force`.

    mikado delete Q12 --journey J1 --rewire Q4      # out of J1 only; Q4 takes over what hung on it
    mikado delete Q12 --journey J1 --force --branch # J1 was its last journey: gone, with its branch
    mikado delete Q12 --force --rewire Q4           # out of every journey and the database
    mikado journey delete J3 [--force]              # --force deletes the quests in no other journey

mikado never asks yes or no: a refused delete changes nothing and names the flag it needs. Add
that flag only when it matches what the user asked for; otherwise tell them what mikado said.

**Look before you change.**

    mikado journey show J1          # the chart: quests, status, requirements, chronicle
    mikado show Q3                  # one quest: what it requires, what it opens, its journeys
    mikado journey show J1 --json   # the same, for you to parse

**Show the user.** `mikado open` opens the dashboard in their browser: the Atlas (its regions), a
region's journeys (`open R2`), a journey's chart (the war table), or the chart with one quest
selected. `--print` gives just the URL, to
paste into a reply.

    mikado open J1
    mikado open Q9 --print

## Commands and flags

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `journey new "title" [--crown Q] [--region R]` | start a journey (in R1 unless a region is named) |
| `journey crown J Q` | make Q the journey's crowning quest |
| `journey set J [--title T] [--crown Q] [--region R]` | retitle, recrown or move a journey (its id stays) |
| `journey list [--all] [--region R]` | the Atlas as text; `--region` keeps one region's journeys |
| `region list` / `region new "name"` / `region set R --name N` | the regions / a new one / rename (its id stays) |
| `region move R J...` | move journeys into R together; refused while a quest on them stays behind on another |
| `region delete R` | delete an empty region (never the last) |
| `journey extract J Q... --title T` | move quests into a new journey, shown on J as one journey card |
| `journey delete J [--force]` | delete a journey; `--force` also deletes its quests in no other journey |
| `add "title" [--url U] [--mark M] [--on WHO]` | add a quest; `--on` makes it a petition |
| `require Q PREREQ` / `unrequire Q PREREQ` | Q requires PREREQ / no longer (either may be a journey id) |
| `rewire Q OLD NEW` | Q requires NEW instead of OLD, in one step |
| `fulfil Q` / `unfulfil Q` | fulfilled / not |
| `take-up Q [--by WHO]` / `set-down Q` | underway / no longer |
| `abandon Q --reason` / `unabandon Q` | won't do / undo that |
| `strike Q --reason` | gone for good, stays only in the chronicle |
| `delete Q (--journey J \| --force) [--branch \| --rewire Q]` | take Q out of J, or out of the database (`--force`; also needed when J is its last journey) |
| `set Q [--title T] [--url U] [--mark M] [--on WHO] [--hero WHO] [--npc=true\|false]` | change it; `-` clears `--url`, `--mark`, `--on` (a plain quest again) or `--hero` |

Link flags on `add`: `--opens Q` (Q requires the new quest), `--requires Q`, `--side-of Q`,
`--crowns J`, `--found-on Q --reason "why"`, `--hero WHO`, `--npc`.

## JSON field names

`--json` output and the API keep plain, older names. Read them as:

| In JSON | Means |
|---|---|
| `status: "done"` | Fulfilled |
| `status: "available"` | Open |
| `status: "locked"` (with `openBefore`: how many to go) | Sealed |
| `status: "awaiting"` | Awaiting reply |
| `status: "cancelled"`, `cancelled`, `cancelReason` | Abandoned, and why |
| journey `state: "complete"` / `"cancelled"` | journey fulfilled / abandoned |
| journey `archivedAt` | archived (absent when not) |
| `kind: "awaiting"`, `waitingOn`, `since` | a Petition, whom it awaits, since when (`kind` is absent on any other quest) |
| `url`, `mark` | its link and mark (absent when not set) |
| `card`, `cards` | a quest, quests |
| `final`, `finalCardId`, `finalOf` | the crowning quest |
| `needs` (`from` requires `to`), `neededBy` | Requires, Opens |
| `sideOf` | a side quest on that quest |
| `foundWhile`, `reason` | found on that quest, and why |
| `working`, `workingBy`, `workingSince` | underway |
| `owner` | the hero |
| `log` | the chronicle |
| `id` / `key` | the quest (`key` is `Q142`); on a journey, `key` is `J7` |
| `crowns` (`key`, `title`, `state`, `done`, `total`, `working`, `open`) | on a chart, a quest that crowns another journey and stands for all of it: that journey's main-quest progress, how many of its quests are underway, and its quests still to do |
| journey `region` (`key`, `name`) | the region it lives in |
| journey `blockedBy` / `blocks` | the journeys drawn on this one's chart as one card each / the journeys with this one on theirs |

## Glossary

The words mikado uses, everywhere a person or an agent reads them.

| # | Word | Meaning | CLI |
|---|---|---|---|
| G1 | Journey | A goal: small enough to finish, big enough to need several quests. It is named by its id, like J7, and drawn as a chart that ends in one crowning quest. | `journey new "title"` |
| G2 | Atlas | The page with every journey at a glance: progress on its main quest, its achievements, and who is on it. | `journey list`, `open` |
| G3 | Chart (war table) | One journey drawn out: every quest on the way to the crowning quest, and what requires what. Another journey this one waits on is drawn as one card, with its progress and a link to its own chart. | `journey show J`, `open J` |
| G4 | Quest (or Task) | Any unit on the chart, named by its id, like Q142: a title, and a status set by hand. "Task" means exactly the same; either word works. | `add "title"`, `show Q` |
| G5 | Link | A quest can carry one link, to anywhere: a recipe, a ticket, a document. Its title in the details opens it, and so does its mark on the chart. | `--url U`, `set Q --url U` |
| G6 | Mark | A short note shown right after a quest's id, at most 15 characters: #13, 234g45a, PROJ-88. It is kept as written, with or without a link. | `--mark M`, `set Q --mark M` |
| G7 | Petition | A quest that awaits a reply from someone, often outside the team, like a production token from a vendor. It says from whom, and since when; without that it is a plain quest again. | `add "title" --on WHO`, `set Q --on WHO` |
| G8 | Crowning quest | The one quest whose fulfilment fulfils the journey. Everything else on the main quest leads to it. | `journey crown J Q`, `--crowns J` |
| G9 | Main quest | The required path: the crowning quest and every quest it requires, directly or not. Its progress is the journey's progress. | |
| G10 | Side quest | Optional polish hung on a quest. It never blocks anything and counts as an achievement, not as progress. | `--side-of Q` |
| G11 | Achievement | What a fulfilled side quest earns: a star beside the journey's progress, never a requirement. | |
| G12 | Requires / Opens | The only blocking link. "Q5 requires Q3" means Q3 must be fulfilled first; said the other way round, Q3 opens Q5. Cycles are refused. | `require Q PREREQ`, `--requires Q`, `--opens Q` |
| G13 | Found | A quest found while working on another, recorded with where and why: "found on Q3: old saves crash the loader". | `--found-on Q --reason "why"` |
| G14 | Fulfilled | Status: finished, when it is marked so. | `fulfil Q` |
| G15 | Open | Status: everything it requires is fulfilled (or abandoned), so it can be started now. | |
| G16 | Sealed | Status: blocked. Something it requires is not fulfilled yet; the badge counts what is left, as in "sealed · 2 to go". | |
| G17 | Awaiting reply | Status of a petition that is otherwise open: only the person it waits on stands in the way. | |
| G18 | Abandoned | Status: won't be done. It stays on the chart, blocks nothing and counts in no total; its side quests are abandoned with it. | `abandon Q --reason "why"`, `unabandon Q` |
| G19 | Struck | Gone for good: taken off the chart with its side quests, and kept only in the chronicle. Prefer abandoning. | `strike Q --reason "why"` |
| G20 | Underway | Someone is on it right now, apart from its status. You take a quest up when you start and set it down when you stop. | `take-up Q [--by WHO]`, `set-down Q` |
| G21 | Hero / no hero | Whoever is responsible for a quest, as set in mikado. A quest without one shows "no hero". | `--hero WHO`, `set Q --hero WHO` |
| G22 | Chronicle | The history: every change as one sentence. A journey's chronicle is its own events plus those of the quests on its chart. | `journey show J` |
| G23 | NPC | A mark any quest can wear. It changes nothing about the quest's status, but NPC quests show in red on the chart; right-click a quest there to mark or unmark it. | `--npc`, `set Q --npc=true\|false` |
| G24 | Archived | A journey put away: off the Atlas's shelves and out of `journey list` (unless `--all`), its chart, quests and chronicle untouched. Archive a journey only when the user asks. | `journey archive J`, `journey unarchive J` |
| G25 | Extract | Moving quests of a journey into a new journey of their own, crowned by a new quest. The old chart shows the new journey as one card where they were. | `journey extract J Q... --title T` |
| G26 | Deleted | Taken out of a journey, or with `--force` out of the database for good (only a line in the chronicle stays). Unlike struck, nothing is kept. Only when the user asks. | `delete Q --journey J`, `delete Q --force`, `journey delete J` |
| G27 | Region | A group of journeys, named by its id, like R2. Every journey lives in one, and a quest stays inside one: no link crosses from one region to another. The Atlas shows the regions; each opens a page of its journeys. | `region new "name"`, `region move R J...`, `--region R` |

## Rules

- Record what you find with `--found-on` and `--reason`. Never add a found quest silently.
- Prefer `abandon` over `strike`. Striking erases a quest from every journey it serves.
- Delete (`delete`, `journey delete`) only when the user asks. Never add `--force`, `--branch`
  or `--rewire` just to get past a refusal: pick the one that matches what the user wants, or ask.
- To move a requirement, use `rewire`, not `unrequire` followed by `require`.
- Do not create issues or tickets in other tools on your own to put them in a journey. Add the
  step as a quest; if it is tracked elsewhere, give it that `--url` and a `--mark`.
- A quest added with no link is in no journey; mikado warns. Link it (`--opens`, `--side-of`,
  `mikado require`) or say why not.
- If a command fails, report mikado's message as it is — it names the quest and the reason
  (for example the cycle a `require` would create).
- Do not start or stop the mikado server; it is the user's.
